text:
Allison Grant: Kicking off a thread on “supported backends” for the Private observability minimum pack. We need to land on a clear support statement for the ADR: Grafana provisioning vs customer-managed Grafana/Prometheus, and what we ship vs what we integrate with. What are we comfortable saying is “supported” vs “works if you wire it yourself”? 

Sergio Costa: From the dashboards/rules side, easiest path is: ship Grafana dashboards as JSON + provisioning manifests (folder, datasource, variables). That can work with either (a) Grafana we deploy or (b) customer Grafana, as long as they let us provision. But “customer-managed” Grafana is a big range (versions, auth modes, locked-down instances). 

Markus Klein: +1. In installs, customers either: 1) already have Prometheus + Grafana and don’t want us running another, or 2) want the “works out of the box” bundle because they don’t have it. If we only support the bundle, we’ll lose a chunk of enterprise Private deals. If we say we support arbitrary customer Grafana, Support will hate us. 

Priya Natarajan: We should separate “supported components” vs “supported integration pattern.” We can support Prometheus metrics + rule format (PrometheusRule) and Grafana dashboards (JSON) as artifacts. Then have two integration modes: Redwood-managed (we deploy) and customer-managed (we hand them artifacts + config). 

Bruno Silva: Installer POV: provisioning Grafana is straightforward if we deploy Grafana (service account, provision datasources, load dashboards). For customer Grafana, we can’t assume network reachability to their Grafana API, especially air-gapped / no cross-namespace access. File-based provisioning requires we can mount files into their Grafana pods, which we can’t. 

Fatima Noor: On-prem reality: many customers run Grafana outside the k8s cluster (VMs) or have it “central.” In air-gapped, they often disallow the installer talking to anything except the cluster API. So if we “require” API provisioning into their Grafana, it will be a blocker. 

Logan Wright: Another angle: we can treat Grafana as optional and focus on: 1) metrics contract (Prometheus scrape), 2) rule bundle (PrometheusRule groups), 3) dashboard JSON artifacts. Then “customer-managed Grafana” support means: we guarantee dashboards are importable and queries are correct, not that we can automate provisioning. 

Nadia Rahman: +1, but we have to be explicit about metric names/labels and versioning. Otherwise dashboards drift. If we publish a versioned pack (v0.1.0 etc), we can say: “Dashboards in vX require metrics contract vY.” 

Sean Gallagher: From SRE: I care that alerts are actually loaded and firing. If we can’t validate rule loading, it’s not supported (we’ll get paged for their bad Prometheus config). For customer-managed Prometheus, at most we can say “we provide rules; you’re responsible for loading them; here’s how to validate with promtool.” But “supported” should probably mean we can run a validation command and get a green check.

Marcus Lin: Security angle: if we deploy Grafana, we own default auth/RBAC defaults and need to be careful: no anonymous auth, secure cookies, TLS, least privilege for service accounts. If customer-managed, we must not demand admin tokens or broad API access. We should avoid “installer needs Grafana admin token” as a baseline.

Naomi Feldman: And for compliance: auditability. If we deploy Grafana/Prometheus, we need a story for audit logs (who changed dashboards/rules). If customer-managed, we can only document what settings they should enable. Either way, we should not put secrets into dashboards or rule annotations.

Allison Grant: So it sounds like we’re leaning towards:
- Officially supported: Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint + PrometheusRule bundle; Grafana dashboards as JSON; optional “Redwood-managed” Grafana/Prometheus deployment for day-1.
- Not officially supported: “we will make your existing Grafana instance accept our provisioning” (too many variants).
But that still leaves: do we ship a Prometheus + Grafana stack as part of the minimum pack or require customer to bring them?

Bruno Silva: If we *require* customer to bring Prometheus/Grafana, we’ll spend time debugging their setup anyway. If we ship them, we can give a consistent experience and validation harness. But then we’re in the business of operating Grafana/Prometheus in Private installs.

Markus Klein: I’d prefer: we ship “batteries included” as the default (in-cluster Prometheus + Grafana), but allow “external mode.” For external, we hand over:
- `dashboards/` JSON bundle
- `prometheus-rules/` YAML
- a config snippet for scrape + relabeling
- a checklist of required recording rules / labels
That’s good enough for enterprise teams with existing platforms.

Sergio Costa: Agree. Also, for external mode: we should standardize on Grafana 10.x JSON export and avoid features that break across versions. Some customers still on Grafana 8.

Logan Wright: I’d rather pin our “supported” customer-managed Grafana versions to a narrow band. Example: “validated on Grafana 9.5+ and 10.x” and best-effort outside that. Otherwise we’ll spend cycles on panel rendering differences.

Ethan Park: Control plane services: if we deploy Grafana/Prometheus, we need to ensure network policies allow scraping the right endpoints across namespaces. For customer-managed, we need docs about which services/ports to scrape and RBAC for ServiceMonitors (if they use Prom Operator). That matrix can get hairy.

Sean Gallagher: Also: Prometheus Operator vs vanilla Prometheus. In k8s, everyone’s on operator. If we support rules, we should write them as `PrometheusRule` CRDs and assume the operator. For non-operator Prometheus, we can provide a rendered rules file, but it’s “best effort.”

Allison Grant: Strong take: support “Prometheus Operator (kube-prometheus-stack)” as the primary path. For air-gapped, we can ship the helm deps pinned and mirrored. For customer-managed Prometheus (non-operator), we can provide a conversion doc but not guarantee.

Fatima Noor: For on-prem packaging: if we depend on kube-prometheus-stack, we need to document image mirroring for all the components. That’s a lot of images. But doable if we pin versions and provide a manifest list.

Connor O'Brien: Release engineering: please please keep the support matrix narrow. If we say “Prometheus Operator + Grafana OSS” that’s at least constrainable. If we say “any SIEM/any Grafana/any Prometheus,” every release becomes a compatibility minefield.

Marcus Lin: Another security point: if we ship Grafana, it needs to integrate with customer IdP (SAML/OIDC) optionally, but we shouldn’t block on that. Default should be local admin user with forced password rotation? Or require they set `GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD` via secret at install time. And we should disable sidecar auto-import from arbitrary configmaps unless we control labeling.

Naomi Feldman: Re: audit logs: Grafana OSS has limited audit logging. Grafana Enterprise has better audit trails. We can’t assume Enterprise. For “supported minimum,” we can document compensating controls: restrict admin access, backup provisioning configs, use GitOps for dashboards/rules. But we should be careful claiming “audit-ready.”

Sergio Costa: Practical: provisioning via config files (mounted dashboards) is more auditable than using Grafana UI imports. If we deploy Grafana, we can set provisioning from ConfigMaps and keep them immutable (or at least versioned). 

Bruno Silva: +1, file-based provisioning works great for our deployed Grafana. For customer-managed Grafana, we can’t mount. So external mode = “import manually / via their pipeline.” That’s ok.

Markus Klein: Support asks will be: “What does Redwood actually support?” Suggest we define:
1) “Redwood-managed stack” (we install Prometheus+Grafana+rules+dashboards) — fully supported.
2) “Customer-managed stack” — we support Redwood metrics endpoints + rules/dashboards artifacts, and we support validation queries, but not their Grafana config.
And we should explicitly state: logs forwarding targets are customer choice; we ship Vector/Fluent Bit config defaults only.

Sean Gallagher: For #2, we should set expectations: Support will ask for proof they loaded rules and can query metrics. We can provide a `redwood-private validate observability` command that runs PromQL queries against their Prometheus endpoint (if reachable) or at least checks our `/metrics` endpoints are alive. If it can’t reach their Prometheus, it only validates “signal emission,” not “signal ingestion.”

Logan Wright: That validation command distinction is important for the ADR. Maybe split it:
- “Emitter validation” = endpoints exist, metrics include required labels, logs are structured.
- “Backend validation” = Prometheus scrape ok, rules loaded, Grafana dashboards provisioned.
Backend validation only possible in Redwood-managed mode.

Allison Grant: This is converging. Let me propose ADR language:
- Supported backends (Primary): Prometheus Operator (PrometheusRule CRDs) + Grafana OSS (self-hosted).
- Supported Redwood integration patterns:
  A) Redwood-managed observability stack (recommended default): installer/helm deploys and provisions Grafana + Prometheus Operator + rules + dashboards.
  B) Customer-managed observability stack (supported artifacts, limited automation): Redwood ships versioned dashboards/rules + configuration guidance; customer is responsible for provisioning/loading; Redwood Support requires passing “Emitter validation” and basic PromQL checks.
- Non-goals: Supporting managed SaaS Grafana Cloud/Datadog/etc directly in min pack (can be “works with” via exporters).
Thoughts?

Priya Natarajan: +1, and add that we’ll keep it flexible by not coupling core runtime to any specific backend. The pack is an integration bundle.

Connor O'Brien: Add version pins:
- kube-prometheus-stack version X
- Grafana version Y
- Prometheus version Z
So release train knows what to test.

Fatima Noor: For air-gap: ADR should mention offline bundle includes all images and helm deps for the Redwood-managed stack. External/customer-managed mode should not require pulling images beyond Redwood core.

Marcus Lin: Also add secure defaults and auth story for the Redwood-managed Grafana: no anonymous, admin password required at install, TLS termination options, and minimal RBAC.

Naomi Feldman: And a note that audit logging depends on customer environment; for OSS Grafana we recommend GitOps provisioning and restricting admin actions; if customer needs audited UI changes, they may need to integrate with their enterprise tooling.

Sergio Costa: One more: dashboards should not rely on Grafana plugins that require internet. Keep to core panels.

Ethan Park: For customer-managed Prometheus Operator, we can ship ServiceMonitor/PodMonitor templates. But supporting “any operator config” is painful. Maybe in external mode we provide scrape config examples (ServiceMonitor) and clearly state namespace/label requirements.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. And for alerting: if customer wants to pipe alerts to their pager (PagerDuty, Opsgenie), we won’t ship that integration in min pack; we’ll provide Alertmanager config examples. Redwood-managed mode should come with sane defaults but not opinionated receivers.

RedwoodBot: :memo: Reminder set by Allison Grant: “Draft ADR for Private observability backend support + integration patterns” in 2 hours.

Allison Grant: Great. I’ll draft ADR-0147 today with this structure and tag folks for review (Security/SRE/Installer/On-prem). Please reply here if you think we’re missing a critical edge case.

Markus Klein: Edge case: some customers run Mimir/Thanos as backend; they still use PromQL and rule format, so artifacts should work. We should avoid saying “Prometheus only,” say “Prometheus-compatible” but *validated* with Prometheus OSS.

Logan Wright: +1. Wording: “Prometheus-compatible metrics + PromQL. Validated on Prometheus OSS via kube-prometheus-stack.”

Priya Natarajan: Works.

Allison Grant: Cool. I’ll make sure ADR separates “validated” vs “theoretical compatibility.”

Sean Gallagher: Also please include paging policy guidance: burn-rate alerts by default, and pipeline health alerts as ticket-level unless sustained.

Allison Grant: Noted — will link to the alerting philosophy doc and keep ADR focused on backend/integration scope.

Connor O'Brien: When you post ADR, include who owns updates to the support matrix (release eng + SRE + Private product), otherwise it will rot.

Allison Grant: Will do. End of thread for now; I’ll post the draft and start a review round.
